speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Has the child had any recent fevers, infections, or been diagnosed with any other illnesses in the past few weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal platelet count and coagulation profile, combined with the specific deficiency of GIIb/IIIa receptors, strongly point to a platelet function disorder. Do you know if there is a family history of bleeding disorders or if the child has had any difficulties with wound healing?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical issues. Up-to-date on vaccinations. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one older sibling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical picture of mucocutaneous bleeding with normal platelet counts and coagulation profiles, specifically combined with the absence of GIIb/IIIa receptors, is diagnostic for Glanzmann thrombasthenia.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
